newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes firm late on heat, Iraq, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes firm late on heat, Iraq, weather.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices held firm late Wednesday, buoyed by a mixed bag of short covering in heating oil, signs of renewed tensions in Iraq and cold weather forecasts, traders said.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $24.45-55 a barrel late in the day, up 60 cents from late Tuesday's cash market.
The March/April WTI spread widened to around 67 cents, up around 14 cents from this morning.
The widening spread drove WTI/Cushing Posting Plus to around $2.35-2.37, with one deal done at $2.36 a barrel.

Grade differnetials were subdued. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James bounced back up to 17-19 cents premium to WTI/Cushing, up from 10-15 cents on Tuesday. A late deal was transacted at 17 cents, traders said.
WTI/Midland also strengthened to 31-35 cents discount to WTI/Cushing, with the grade changing hands late at minus 34 cents.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire traded at minus 40 cents, about even with Tuesday's range.
West Texas Sour/Midland was also steady, with one deal done at WTI/Cushing minus $1.85 a barrel.
On other sour grades, lightly traded Eugene Island was heard done at discounts of $1.60 and $1.70 a barrel, down from a range of $1.45-1.60 on Tuesday.
Bonito Sour was heard done at minus $1.37 a barrel, also weaker.

The grades have bounced back and forth in recent days, partly in response to the influx of foreign crudes. The WTI/Brent spread narrowed Wednesday while CFD and dated Brent climbed, raising the price for transatlantic cargoes into the Gulf Coast, traders said.
The going price is now around WTI minus 20-25 cents, up from a discount of 30-40 cents few days ago, traders said.
The price increase has boosted the appeal of alternative domestic grades such as LLS.
